selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs on node1
selected_evidence.summary: /etc/cron.allow contains exactly root and opsadmin with secure ownership and permissions. Live checks accept both listed accounts and reject an unlisted account, including after reboot.

Healthy baseline boot ID 03408ac4-bfe4-4151-98bd-1966b0a205af was captured, the native reboot was acknowledged, and node1 returned with changed boot ID c0c9c8ec-7288-4675-91bc-f66e49468adf. Post-restart system state is running, crond is enabled and active, opsadmin exists, and the access policy remains effective.

commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf 'crond_active='; systemctl is-active crond
printf '%s\n' '--- /etc/cron.allow ---'
if [ -e /etc/cron.allow ]; then stat -c 'mode=%a owner=%U group=%G' /etc/cron.allow; sed -n '1,20p' /etc/cron.allow; else printf '%s\n' 'MISSING'; fi
printf '%s\n' '--- /etc/cron.deny ---'
if [ -e /etc/cron.deny ]; then stat -c 'mode=%a owner=%U group=%G' /etc/cron.deny; sed -n '1,20p' /etc/cron.deny; else printf '%s\n' 'MISSING'; fi
printf '%s\n' '--- accounts ---'
getent passwd root opsadmin || true

commands.command:
set -eu
if ! getent passwd opsadmin >/dev/null; then useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash opsadmin; fi
getent passwd opsadmin
stat -c 'home_mode=%a owner=%U group=%G' /home/opsadmin

set -eu
allow_tmp=$(mktemp /etc/cron.allow.XXXXXX)
printf '%s\n' root opsadmin > "$allow_tmp"
chown root:root "$allow_tmp"
chmod 0600 "$allow_tmp"
mv -f "$allow_tmp" /etc/cron.allow
restorecon /etc/cron.allow 2>/dev/null || true
stat -c 'mode=%a owner=%U group=%G context=%C' /etc/cron.allow
sed -n '1,10p' /etc/cron.allow
commands.stdout:
mode=600 owner=root group=root context=system_u:object_r:etc_t:s0
root
opsadmin

commands.command:
set -u
check_user() {
  user_name=$1
  out_file=$(mktemp)
  runuser -u "$user_name" -- crontab -l >"$out_file" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  printf 'user=%s rc=%s output=' "$user_name" "$rc"
  tr '\n' ' ' <"$out_file"
  printf '\n'
  rm -f "$out_file"
}
check_user root
check_user opsadmin
check_user nobody
printf 'crond_active='; systemctl is-active crond
printf '%s\n' 'allow_file:'
stat -c 'mode=%a owner=%U group=%G' /etc/cron.allow
cat /etc/cron.allow
commands.stdout:
user=root rc=1 output=no crontab for root 
user=opsadmin rc=1 output=no crontab for opsadmin 
user=nobody rc=1 output=You (nobody) are not allowed to use this program (crontab) See crontab(1) for more information 
crond_active=active
allow_file:
mode=600 owner=root group=root
root
opsadmin
